blocks.text: JavaScript Temporal PlainDate
The Temporal.PlainDate Object
The Temporal.PlainDate object represents a calendar date without a time.
A Temporal.PlainDate is typically in ISO 8601 format (2026-05-01).

It is easier to use and safer to compare than DateTime objects for dates that are the same
regardless of time zone, such as birthdays and holidays.
How to Create a PlainDate Object
An PlainDateTime object can be created in several different ways:
Create a PlainDate with new
You can create a PlainDate object using the new constructor.
The constructor takes year, month, and day parameters.

// Create a PlainDate object

const date = new Temporal.PlainDate(2026, 5, 17);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Temporal.PlainDate() method above:

items: Returns a calendar date without a time like 2026-05-17.

blocks.text: Unlike JavaScript Date, Temporal months start at 1.
Create a PlainDate from a String

You can create a PlainDate object from an
ISO 8601 / RFC 9557 string.

// Create a PlainDate object

const date = Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-05-17");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: In the example above:

items: The input is parsed using ISO 8601 parsing rules

blocks.text: Parsing means validation pluss automatic conversion.
Create a PlainDate from an Object
You can create a PlainDate object from an object.

// Create a PlainDate object

const date = Temporal.PlainDate.from({year:2026, month:5, day:1});
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
From the example above, you can reason that the from() method can accept
both object literals and PlainDate objects.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Create a PlainDate Object from Now
The Temporal.Now object has a method for getting the current date:
let today = Temporal.Now.plainDateISO();
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The Temporal.Now.plainDateISO() method is used to get the current date.

It returns a PlainDate object with the (year, month, day)
in the ISO 8601 calendar, specifically ignoring time zones and times.

blocks.text: Add and Subtract Days
Use the add() method to add time.

let date = Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-05-17");

let nextWeek = date.add({ days: 7 });
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Use the subtract() method to subtract time.

let date = Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-05-17");

let previousWeek = date.subtract({ days: 7 });
blocks.caption: Example

manually using milliseconds.

blocks.caption: Date Example

blocks.text: Temporal provides methods that are clearer and safer than using JavaScript Date methods.
JavaScript Temporal since()
The since() method calculates the duration between two temporal dates.
t1.since(t2, options)
blocks.caption: Syntax

blocks.text: Meaning:
At time t1, how much time has passed since time t2?

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
The since() method returns a Temporal.Duration Object
representing the elapsed time.
The duration is positive if the "other" date is in the past.
The duration is negative if the "other" date is in the future.

blocks.text: Temporal Calendars
Temporal.PlainDate defaults to the ISO 8601 calendar.
If you want a specific calendar, you can add a calender parameter:
new Temporal.PlainDate(2026, 5, 17, "gregory")
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
The from() method supports calendars using the [u-ca=calendar] syntax or a calendar
property in objects.
Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-05-17[u-ca=chinese]")
blocks.caption: Examples

blocks.text: Temporal.PlainDate.from({year:2026, month:5, day:17, calendar:"hebrew"})
blocks.caption: Examples

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: When to Use PlainDate
Replace Date for Date-Only Values
With Date, you always get a time and time zone.
This can create confusion when you only need a calendar date.
let d = new Date("2026-05-17");
blocks.caption: Date Example

blocks.text: PlainDate avoids this by storing only year, month, and day.
